sections.h2: Where is Swatara Township, and what is it like to sell a house there?
sections.html:
Swatara Township is a Dauphin County township just south of Susquehanna Township in the Harrisburg area, and selling a house there means working with a township codes office, a private real estate tax collector and the county recorder. The township's municipal building is at 599 Eisenhower Boulevard in Harrisburg.

A 1799 court order split Lower Paxton Township in two and the southern half took the name Swatara, from Swatara Creek. The word is thought to come from a Susquehannock term meaning where we fed on eels. The township covers 15.5 square miles, with 13.05 of land and nearly 16 percent water along the Susquehanna River, and it holds Calver Island, which was added to the National Register in 2007.

sections.h2: Which communities and numbers define Swatara Township?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 27,936 residents on July 1, 2025, up from 23,362 in 2010 and 27,824 in the 2020 count. Population density is about 2,132 people per square mile.

Owners occupy 69.9 percent of homes, and the middle owned home was valued at $214,400 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $1,252 and median household income is $80,444. The township has 10,640 households averaging 2.47 people, and 17.2 percent of residents were born abroad, with 24.7 percent speaking a language other than English at home.

  • Named places: Bressler, Enhaut, Oberlin, Lawnton and Rutherford are census-designated places inside the township.
  • Retail and logistics: 2022 retail sales reached $1,147,259,000, or $41,104 per resident, and transportation and warehousing receipts were $509,815,000, the largest figure reported among the four places in this comparison.
  • Education: 87.5 percent of adults 25 and over hold a high school diploma, and 28.5 percent hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

sections.h2: What do Swatara's Building and Codes rules mean for a seller?
sections.html:
The Building and Codes Department issues building and zoning permits, and the township uses Approved Code Services, Inc. as an exclusive third-party agency for plan reviews and construction inspections. The same department enforces the International Property Maintenance Code and responds to complaints about property maintenance.

Building permits are generally required for new construction, additions and alterations. They are generally not needed for routine maintenance and repair of buildings or replacement of existing equipment. The department also handles stormwater management permits and requests for exemption from the quarterly waste management fee in certain situations.

If a buyer's lender or inspector flags unpermitted work, call the department at 717-564-2551 before you respond. The office is open weekdays from 8 until 4:30. The township holds a fall brush collection each year, and the 2026 round ran the week of September 21 to 26, which is a useful time to clear yard waste before showing a property.

sections.h2: Who collects real estate tax in Swatara, and what does closing cost in transfer tax?
sections.html:
Swatara Township has its own real estate tax collector, located at 6400A Chambers Hill Road in Harrisburg, separate from the municipal building. The township says real estate payments are accepted for the current year only and that the municipal building does not take them. Requests for tax certifications go to the collector's office, phone 717-832-4908.

Local services tax and earned income tax are collected by Keystone Collections Group instead, with a Dauphin County office on Vartan Way. That split is useful to know when a title agent asks which office issues which certificate.

The recorder's FAQ describes this 2 percent as split between the state, the municipality and the school district. Deeds are recorded at the Dauphin County Courthouse, Room 102, 101 Market Street, Harrisburg, and the county holds deeds from 1785 forward.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads will Swatara buyers care about?
sections.html:
Central Dauphin School District serves Swatara Township, along with Lower Paxton, Middle Paxton and West Hanover townships and the boroughs of Dauphin, Paxtang and Penbrook. The district lists Swatara Middle School among its middle schools, and Lawnton Elementary, Rutherford Elementary and Chambers Hill Elementary among its elementary schools. It is the largest district in the county and the ninth largest in Pennsylvania.

Commutes average 20 minutes. The township reaches the Susquehanna River and is named for Swatara Creek, so a house near the water can raise questions that an interior lot does not. Ask your agent or a surveyor to confirm flood zone status if the property sits close to the creek or the river.

sections.h2: What should you collect before closing a Swatara Township sale?
sections.html:
A clean closing depends on a short list of documents, and most of them come from offices named on this page.

  • A tax certification from the township's real estate tax collector, so the title agent knows what is paid for the current year.
  • A payoff letter from your lender, plus the deed copy from the Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds.
  • Permit records for any addition, deck or alteration, from the Building and Codes Department.
  • Sewer and stormwater bills, which the township lists on a separate online payment page from real estate tax.
  • Receipts for work done since you bought, because buyers who finance will have an appraiser and an inspector look at condition.

About 88.3 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so many Swatara owners have held their homes for a long time and may be unfamiliar with current paperwork. Younger households and older ones both shop here: 19.3 percent of residents are under 18, and 15.4 percent are 65 or older. Broadband reaches 93.0 percent of households, which matters if a buyer works from home.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Swatara Township house fast?
sections.html:
The main routes are a traditional listing, a private sale and a direct purchase by an investor or cash buyer. A listing can bring in the highest price but ties you to showings, repair requests and a lender's timeline.

  • Listing: best for a house in good condition where you can wait on financing and inspections.
  • Private sale: saves a commission but leaves the paperwork and pricing to you.
  • Direct purchase: removes financing and showings and allows closing on your date, with the price reflecting repair needs.

With any route, get a tax certification from the collector, a payoff statement from your lender and a copy of the deed. Ask each buyer in writing who pays the 2 percent transfer tax, since the deed will not record until it is paid.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Swatara Township real estate tax?
faqs.a: At the township's real estate tax collector at 6400A Chambers Hill Road, Harrisburg, or online through the link on the township's tax page. The municipal building does not accept real estate tax payments.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax do I owe selling in Swatara Township?
faqs.a: The Dauphin County recorder describes a 2 percent tax, with 1 percent to the state and one half percent each to the municipality and school district. On the $214,400 Census median value, that is $4,288.

faqs.q: Does Swatara Township require permits for repairs before a sale?
faqs.a: New construction, additions and alterations generally need a building permit, while routine maintenance and replacement of existing equipment generally do not. Call the Building and Codes Department at 717-564-2551 if you are unsure.

faqs.q: Who collects Swatara's local services and earned income taxes?
faqs.a: Keystone Collections Group, which keeps a Dauphin County office on Vartan Way in Harrisburg. This is separate from the real estate tax collector.

faqs.q: Which school district is Swatara Township in?
faqs.a: Central Dauphin School District. Its list of schools includes Swatara Middle School and elementary schools in Lawnton, Rutherford and Chambers Hill.
